findings.evidence: Lines 72–73 define the predicate using `∃ x y, x ≠ y ∧ ...`, while lines 92–95 explicitly describe its negation as no row meeting a column “twice”; theorem names should describe their conclusions in standard terminology.
findings.fix: Rename the predicate to something explicit such as `RowMeetsColumnTwice` (or a standard collision/intersection-cardinality term) and consistently rename declarations at lines 78, 86, 95, 103, 162, 195, 209, and 230.
findings.issue: `RowMeetsColumn` means that a row and column share at least two distinct labels, not merely that they meet; indeed `not_rowMeetsColumn_self` proves it false even though every occupied row meets a column once. All derived `rowMeetsColumn` declaration names inherit this misleading terminology.

findings.evidence: Lines 170–173 conclude an equality with `((Equiv.Perm.sign q : ℤ) : ℚ) • youngSymmetrizer t`; the naming guide requires descriptive names read from the conclusion outward and uses `_of_` for hypotheses.
findings.fix: Rename it to describe the equality outward, for example `rowSymmetrizer_mul_single_mul_columnAntisymmetrizer_eq_sign_smul_of_mem_rowSubgroup_of_mem_colSubgroup`.
findings.issue: `rowSymmetrizer_mul_single_mul_columnAntisymmetrizer_of_mul_mem` names only its hypotheses and omits the substantive conclusion that the sandwich equals `sign q • youngSymmetrizer t`; `mul_mem` also suggests one membership assertion, whereas the theorem takes separate row- and column-subgroup memberships.

summary: The central predicate and one equality theorem have names that do not accurately describe their statements.
